content: Taking multiple medications with abacavir can lead to an overdose. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For less severe cases, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of abacavir, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store abacavir tablets or solution at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The solution can also be stored in the refrigerator but should not be frozen. Over time, the solution may change color from clear or yellow to brown, which is normal. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about abacavir. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Abacavir may increase the risk of heart attack. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of this treatment with your doctor, as well as strategies to reduce your risk of heart disease. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant before starting this medication, as treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Be aware that this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Abacavir should not be taken with other medications that also contain abacavir. Always check the labels of your other prescription medications to confirm they do not include this ingredient. If you are adding plans to compare formulary information for abacavir or other drugs in the same class, create a list of plans to view and save this information. Keep in mind that individual plans may vary, and formulary details can change. Contact the relevant plan provider for the most up-to-date information.
